\section[l'elettricità]{l'elettricità — electricity}

\label{lesson:IT-C201-elettricita}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for a lawn, then the Italian for a path.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: l'elettricità}
\textbf{l'elettricità} — \textquotedblleft{}electricity\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{elettricità} — built from the word for \textquotedblleft{}electric\textquotedblright{} with \emph{-ità}, \textquotedblleft{}-ness\textquotedblright{}. That word goes back to Latin \emph{electrum}, \textquotedblleft{}amber\textquotedblright{}, from Greek \emph{elektron}: rubbed amber gives a spark. (EtymDB 2.1 records the Latin and Greek words.)
\end{cousinweb}

\end{grammarlens}
